source.title: On the Versatility of Sparse Autoencoders for In-Context Learning
source.authors: Ikhyun Cho; Gaeul Kwon; J. Hockenmaier

record.tranche_reason: The study uses SAE reconstruction loss as a signal for selecting ICL prompts and reports results for that application. It does not test the claim versions about the structure, scaling, function, or training artifacts of SAE error.
record.gate_note: The study reports qualitative relationships between SAE reconstruction loss and ICL task difficulty/performance (Figures 2a–d), recorded below as findings about the measured loss that none of the versions specifically cover. SAE-GPS, flipped SAE-GPS, and baseline performance comparisons are results of the study's new prompt-selection method, not direct measurements of the claim versions, so they are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses SAE reconstruction loss as an unsupervised signal for ICL prompt selection and correlates it with task accuracy. It does not measure linear predictability of the error, scaling across SAE sizes, loss impact versus random errors, the decomposition of the error, or the effect of dropping the error term in circuits or steering. It also does not compare training methods. Its correlational findings concern a different construct (reconstruction loss as a performance proxy).
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that SAE reconstruction loss is informative for ICL: it correlates strongly with performance, separates easy from hard examples, and supports unsupervised prompt selection (SAE-GPS) across Gemma2-9B-IT and Llama3-8B-Instruct. It also tracks multilingual performance.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses SAE reconstruction loss as an ICL prompt-selection and performance signal; it does not perform the original study's analyses of SAE error structure or scaling.
record.method_sensitivity: For SAE-GPS performance on Gemma2-9B-IT, the reported results vary by layer: layers 28 and 32 outperform layer 42 on the reported Rest14 and Lap14 results. This concerns the prompt-selection method, not a tested claim version.

fits_no_version.finding: On Rest14 (Gemma2-9B-IT, layer 32 SAE), easy examples have lower SAE reconstruction loss than non-trivial ones.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE reconstruction error magnitude varies with input difficulty for the model.

fits_no_version.finding: Higher prompt-level and corpus-level SAE reconstruction loss is associated with higher ICL accuracy; selecting the highest-loss prompt improves accuracy over majority vote. The flipped (lowest-loss) selection does worse.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE reconstruction error norm tracks the information richness of activations and predicts downstream task performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 14 M-MMLU languages, SAE reconstruction loss correlates strongly with accuracy; higher-resource languages have higher loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE reconstruction error is larger for inputs or languages the model handles more capably.

record.peer_reviewed: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2025
record.problems: The reported relationships in Figures 2(a)–(d) are qualitative in the text, without numerical correlation coefficients or uncertainty estimates. The example-level analysis uses 20 randomly selected prompts. The study's limitations note reliance on publicly available SAEs and restricted model coverage.
record.rows_left_out: No direct claim-version results were reported. SAE-GPS and flipped SAE-GPS accuracy results and comparisons with ICL and KATE, in Tables 1–3, were left out because they evaluate the study's prompt-selection method rather than the claim's SAE-error properties.

untested.parts: Whether the error vector is linearly predictable from the input activation; not tested.
Error norm predictability across SAE sizes, shared failure contexts, and persistence with scale; not tested (only one SAE width used).
Loss impact of splicing in reconstructions versus random errors; not tested.
Split of the error into linear and nonlinear components; not tested.
Loss of behaviour in circuit or steering analyses without the error term; not tested.
Dependence of the error on the training method or architecture; not tested.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T4 classification is right. The rows are figure-only correlations of the error norm with accuracy and bear on no version. They are loosely adjacent to V2 (per-context error variation), but the study uses no SAE-size comparison. The Limitations section says experiments are limited to Gemma2, yet Tables 2–3 include Llama3-8B-Instruct (layer 25 SAE); this is an internal inconsistency.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of SAE error is a linear function of the input activation.
Whether per-token error norms are predictable across SAE sizes, whether larger SAEs fail on the same contexts, and whether error persists with scale.
Whether SAE reconstruction errors harm model loss more than random errors of the same size.
Whether SAE error separates into a linear part containing unlearned features and a qualitatively distinct nonlinear part resistant to dictionary learning.
Whether SAE-based circuit or steering analyses lose model behavior when the error term is omitted.
Whether dark matter is mainly an SAE-training artifact and shrinks with improved architectures or end-to-end training.
